summary: Agent lanes shows several agents working on one job, each in its own row with a name, what it is doing right now, a step track and a status tag. When one agent passes work to another, a banner like "Researcher handed the brief to Designer" slides in above the lane that takes it.
use: When your product runs several agents with different roles, like a researcher, a designer and a reviewer, on one task.
When some agents wait on others and people need to see who is blocked and why.
When people should be able to pause every agent at once and resume them later.
When each agent's own log should be one click away without crowding the overview.
features: Each lane has a `status`: queued, waiting, working, paused or done. Working shows a spinner, paused holds, and done settles with a check.
The `activity` line crossfades when it changes. The track is cut into `steps` (3 by default), and the step after `done` fills while the agent works.
Clicking a lane opens its `log`, with an optional time for each entry. Open lanes can be controlled with `expanded` and `onExpandedChange`.
Setting `handoff` to `{ from, to, what }` slides a banner in above the receiving lane. Set it back to undefined and the banner slides away.
The header reads "3 agents working", "All agents paused" or "All 3 agents finished" unless you pass `title`, and shows a m:ss clock that counts while agents work.
`onPausedChange` adds a Pause all / Resume button that turns working lanes into Paused and stops the clock. It disappears once every lane is done.
a11y: Each lane row is a button with `aria-expanded` for its log.
Closed logs and a hand-off banner that is leaving are `inert` and `aria-hidden`.
The working spinner is `aria-hidden`, and each status is written out as text, like Working, Paused or Done.

faq.q: Does Pause all stop my agents?
faq.a: No. It changes how the lanes look and calls `onPausedChange`. Your code pauses the agents, and the lanes' own `status` values stay as you set them.

faq.q: How do I show one agent handing work to another?
faq.a: Set `handoff` with the `from` and `to` lane keys and a short `what`, like "the brief". Clear it after a moment and the banner closes before it goes.

faq.q: Can a lane have more than three steps?
faq.a: Yes. Set `steps` on the lane to cut its track into as many parts as you need, and move `done` forward as each one finishes.
